# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## I. PLACEMENT GAMES
Games where you place objects, numbers, or symbols in cells

### A. Light/Illumination
- **Akari** - Place light bulbs that illuminate rows/columns

### B. Number Placement
- **Sudoku** - Place numbers 1-9 in rows, columns, and blocks
- **Nansuke** - Fill blank cells with numbers from a list
- **Makaro** - Fill cells with numbers based on directional arrow constraints
- **Ripple Effect** - Fill rooms with consecutive numbers starting from 1
- **Kurotto** - Color cells based on number constraints in circles

### C. Shape/Block Placement
- **Shikaku** - Divide grid into rectangles containing one number
- **Fillomino** - Fill blocks with numbers matching block size
- **Chained Block** - Fill blocks with numbers, forming chains
- **LITS** - Place tetrominoes in regions
- **Evolomino** - Place squares on arrows with progressive growth
- **Pencils** - Draw lines from pencil tips with specified lengths
- **Sashigane** - Divide grid into L-shaped blocks

### D. Circle/Object Movement
- **Satogaeri** - Move circles so each country contains one
- **Yosenabe** - Move circles into gray areas with sum constraints

## II. COLORING/SHADING GAMES
Games where you color or shade cells

### A. Black Cell Placement
- **Kurodoko** - Color cells black based on distance constraints
- **Hitori** - Color cells to eliminate duplicate numbers in rows/columns
- **Nurikabe** - Color cells to form continuous black wall with white regions
- **Nurimisaki** - Color cells with white "promontory" constraints
- **Usowan** - Color cells with one wrong number per region
- **Sto-stone** - Color cells that "drop" to fill bottom half
- **Tilepaint** - Color tiles based on diagonal number constraints
- **Norinori** - Color cells in pairs within regions

### B. Mixed Coloring
- **Heyawake** - Color cells in rooms with connectivity constraints
- **Nuritwin** - Shade two equal-sized blocks per region
- **Double Choco** - Divide blocks with matching white/gray pairs
- **Shakashaka** - Place triangles creating white rectangles/squares
- **Choco Banana** - Color cells so black forms rectangles, white doesn't

## III. LINE-DRAWING GAMES
Games where you draw continuous lines or loops

### A. Single Loop Games
- **Masyu** - Loop through white and black circles with turn rules
- **Slitherlink** - Connect dots to form loop with number constraints
- **Dotchi-Loop** - Loop through white circles with area-based turn rules
- **Nagareru** - Loop following arrow directions with wind constraints
- **Suraromu** - Loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing gates
- **Moon-or-Sun** - Loop alternating between moon/sun cells per room
- **Yajilin** - Loop avoiding black cells indicated by arrows
- **Mid-loop** - Loop with black circles as midpoints of segments

### B. Path/Connection Games
- **Numberlink** - Connect pairs of same numbers with non-crossing lines
- **Hashiwokakero** - Connect islands with bridges (up to 2 per pair)

## IV. DIVISION/PARTITIONING GAMES
Games where you divide the grid into regions

### A. Region Division
- **Five Cells** - Divide into 5-cell blocks with line constraints
- **Nurimeizu** - Create maze from S to G with room-based walls

## V. HYBRID GAMES
Games combining multiple mechanics

- **Hebi** - Place sequential numbers (1-5) forming snakes with visibility rules
- **Juosan** - Fill cells with dashes/pipes with directional extension limits

---

## Summary by Primary Mechanic

| Mechanic | Count | Examples |
|----------|-------|----------|
| **Coloring** | 14 | Kurodoko, Hitori, Nurikabe, etc. |
| **Line Drawing** | 8 | Masyu, Slitherlink, Dotchi-Loop, etc. |
| **Number Placement** | 4 | Sudoku, Nansuke, Makaro, Ripple Effect |
| **Shape Placement** | 7 | Shikaku, Fillomino, LITS, etc. |
| **Division** | 2 | Five Cells, Nurimeizu |
| **Movement** | 2 | Satogaeri, Yosenabe |
| **Hybrid** | 2 | Hebi, Juosan |
